text:
mike: seeing weird reconnection loops from EU users today — client reconnects quickly after a 204 from the edge and console shows duplicate consumption. anyone else?
anya: 204? that should be no body. which proxy/version?
mike: eu-edge v2 canary. header snapshot in logs shows Content-Type: text/event-stream + status=204. clients interpret as EOF and reconnect.
shrey: pasted reproduction steps: cause is our proxy normalization when runtime sends an empty keepalive (we converted to 204 to shave bytes). some SDKs close on non-200.
katie: that mismatch is the root. browsers/ios treat 204 as terminal; SSE expects open stream.
mike: outcome is resume succeeds on reconnect and billing counts tokens twice. bad.
shrey: quick plan: stop normalizing empty keepalives to 204. instead emit a comment event ":keepalive

" and keep status 200. I'll prepare a canary patch.
anya: also add billing-side protection: dedupe resume events by (tenant,resume_id,last_event_id) for a short TTL (10s) so transient dupes don't bill twice.
katie: console changes: surface a route-level metric `keepalive_status_overrides` and a dashboard badge. add alert at 0.5% request rate in a minute window.
mike: can we hotfix tonight to reduce impact for affected customers?
shrey: I can push canary tonight and promote if checks pass. PRs: proxy https://git.redwood/s/proxy/pulls/458, billing https://git.redwood/s/billing/pulls/112 (drafts).
anya: small SDK note: for now advise clients that 204 should be treated as terminal; we'll make server behavior consistent soon. add to changelog.
deploy-bot: Canary eu-edge v2 deploy started at 1769999940, 12% traffic. Canary promoted to 50% at 1769999995.
katie: created alert rule ID STR-204-KA and dashboard panel for "Keepalive mismatches". linking traces. tagging console oncall.
mike: I'll open an incident and notify reporters. watching for dup charge spikes. thanks team :thumbsup:
